section: Theorem 2, the tilt identity, for a finite killed chain (rigour/THEOREMS.md; mathlib/GumpMath/Chain*.lean)
rows: tilt_identity
THEOREMS.md, Theorem 2: for S(G) under (K), with μ_s ∝ μ e^{-sE}: ln τ = ∫₀¹⟨E⟩_s ds = Σ_i c_i, c_i = ∫₀¹⟨ε_i⟩_s ds; s ↦ ⟨E⟩_s is non-increasing, so ⟨E⟩₁ ≤ ln τ ≤ ⟨E⟩₀.

Stronger in scope: any finite killed chain whose one-step death probability is a product of local factors in (0, 1] (that is (K) with the product kernel), and any quasi-stationary law μ (a probability row vector with μQ = λμ). τ is defined as Σ_t P_μ(T > t) with P_μ(T > t) = Σ_y (μQ^t)_y; the path space is not constructed. The surrogate enters by instantiation (tilt_identity_product).
neg_log_Z_one
the analytic core of Theorem 2 (the referee's reading (i)): -ln E_μ e^{-E} = ∫₀¹ ⟨E⟩_s ds for any probability vector and any real E.
Same. Z(s) is a finite sum of exponentials: no eigenvalue perturbation theory is needed.
IsQSD.lifetime_eq
Lemma 0 / Theorem 2's proof: τ = E_μ T = 1/h with h = Σ μ d = 1 - λ.
Same, with E_μ T := Σ_t P_μ(T > t); IsQSD.survival_eq gives P_μ(T > t) = λ^t.
IsQSD.last_living_law
Theorem 2: μ₁(x) = μ(x) d(x)/h is the law of the last living state X_{T-1} under P_μ.
Same, with P_μ(X_{T-1} = x) written as Σ_t P_μ(X_t = x) d(x).
price_mem
Theorem 2: c_i ∈ [0, ε_max].
Same.
exists_qsd
(used silently by Theorem 2 on hull faces and strips, where Lemma 0 is not proved) a quasi-stationary law exists.

New, and the law is identified (IsDominantQSD, repair D2): every finite killed chain on a nonempty set has a quasi-stationary law whose λ is maximal among all quasi-stationary laws, at least Q u u for every state u, and the exponential decay rate of the longest-lived start (P_x(T > t) ≤ C_ε(λ+ε)^t for all x, ≥ λ^t for some x at each t). So the λ = 0 point mass on a surely-dying state is excluded wherever a state can persist. That λ is the spectral radius is not stated beyond this.
tilt_identity_exists
Theorem 2 on every face, wrapped or rimmed.
For the dominant law (IsDominantQSD); also ln τ ≤ E_μ[E] (Theorem 1) and τ ≥ 1/(1 − Q u u) for every u. Uniqueness is not claimed where Lemma 0 is not available (hull faces, strips).
tilt_identity_product
Theorem 2 for S(G): the surrogate's kernel is a product over cells with (K).

For every product kernel P(x, y) = Π_i (a_i(x) if i ∈ y else 1 − a_i(x)) with 0 ≤ a_i < 1, for the dominant QSD, with the local factors the cells' own 1 − a_i (G.localDeath, named); also ln τ ≤ E_μ[E] and τ ≥ 1/(1 − Q u u). The surrogate's a_i (coins and B45/S345) is supplied by the instantiation; ChainCoins.lean has the one-cell law.
price_invariant
Theorem 2: on a wrapped face c_i depends only on the orientation of i; c_X = c_Y = c_Z on tori invariant under the rotation by 2π/3.

For any permutation g of states preserving Q and π of cells carrying the local factors along, given that the quasi-stationary law with λ > 0 is unique. Discharged in Lean for the translations (kagome_one_price) and the rotation by 2π/3 (kagome_rotation).
kagome_one_price
THEOREMS.md, Theorem 2: on a wrapped face c_i depends only on the orientation of i, so ln τ(Λ) = (A/3)(c_X + c_Y + c_Z).

Same, for the surrogate on the kagome layer over every finite abelian group generated by e1, e2 (A = 3|T|), for the unique QSD with λ > 0; proved from Lemma 0 (kagome_lemma0) and the translations. The rotation clause is kagome_rotation.
kagome_rotation
THEOREMS.md, Theorem 2: c_X = c_Y = c_Z when Λ is invariant under the rotation by 2π/3 (equilateral tori): one price per cell.
Same, with the invariance stated as an automorphism R of T with R e1 = -e2, R e2 = e1 - e2 (the rotation (x,y,z) ↦ (y,z,x) of the layer); then ln τ = 3|T|·c.
exists_pos_eigenvector
(the brief) a positive eigenvector of an irreducible non-negative matrix on a finite set.
Same, with a non-negative eigenvalue (Wielandt's proof). That this eigenvalue is the spectral radius is not proved; left_eigenvalue_eq shows every probability row eigenvector has it.
left_eigen_unique
Darroch–Seneta's ingredient: the quasi-stationary law of an irreducible chain is unique.
Same: two probability row eigenvectors of an irreducible non-negative matrix are equal and have the same eigenvalue.
qsd_exists_unique
Lemma 0 ⇒ the quasi-stationary law μ is unique and charges every non-empty state.

Uniqueness among laws with λ > 0. Lean's IsQSD is only the eigen-equation μQ = λμ, under which the point mass at a surely-dying state (the all-alive wrapped face) is a solution with λ = 0; under the standard definition of a QSD (P_μ(T > t) > 0 for all t, i.e. λ > 0) the source's statement is right as written.
decay_bounds
Lemma 0 / Darroch–Seneta: from the quasi-stationary law the death time is geometric with ratio λ; the source's τ is meant as the lifetime of a face.

New: from every state x of the living class, (m/M)λ^t ≤ P_x(T > t) and P_x(T > t+1) ≤ (M/m)λ^t, m ≤ w ≤ M the Perron column vector, and every QSD with λ > 0 has this λ. So the decay rate from every start is λ.
lifetime_from_bounds
(the tie between τ = E_μ T and a lifetime measured from a fair start)

New: conditional on r < 1 (an implication in the theorem): (m/M)/(1−λ) ≤ E_x T ≤ 1 + (M/m)/(1−λ) for x in the class; ln E_x T = ln τ up to ln(M/m) + O(1). The spread M/m is not bounded. lifetime_from_bounds_K proves r < 1 from (K).
lifetime_from_bounds_K
(the tie between τ and a lifetime from a start, unconditional)
As lifetime_from_bounds with λ < 1 proved from (K): every state dies with positive probability.

ln τ ≤ -ln min(ρ1²ρ2,(1-ρ1)²(1-ρ2))·A for every QSD of the surrogate on the kagome layer over T, A = 3|T|; with emax_main, ≤ 2.51·A at (0.44, 0.42).
kagome_sharp_bound
ref-chain/REVIEW.md D7 (the referee's paper proof): ln τ ≤ (2ε_max + ε₂)/3·A = 2.2411·A on wrapped faces.

Same argument, for every QSD of the surrogate on the kagome layer over any finite T at (0.44, 0.42), proved as ≤ 2.2412·A (the constant is 2.241096). Ingredients: indeg (every cell is the neighbour of six slots), card_S_le (3|S| ≤ 2A), energy_le_sharp. Not for hull faces. The dice agent's Gump.Dice.lntau_le_regular (ln τ < 1.9228·A on its faces proved regular) is a separate theorem about Gump.Dice.Face.
kagome_lemma0

THEOREMS.md, Lemma 0 (wrapped faces), geometry included: one living class, aperiodic at u = the X cells, the rest dies surely and is reachable from u; hence the QSD is unique and charges every non-empty state.

For the surrogate with three coins per cell (0 < ρ1, ρ2 < 1) on the kagome layer over any finite abelian group T generated by e1, e2 (every wrapped face (H,K),(0,D) is T = ℤ²/⟨(H,K),(0,D)⟩), neighbours with multiplicity. The neighbour lists were checked against reference/oracle.py's offsets by a script (notes/chain.md), not in Lean; that this layer is the other agent's `torus` face is not proved. Uniqueness among λ > 0. Step (4) is proved by a different route (Y and Z detours) from the source's line growth.
one_class
THEOREMS.md, Lemma 0 and its consequence: one living class, so the quasi-stationary law is unique and charges every non-empty state.

Abstract form, for any finite killed chain: if some living state u leads to every living state in one step (step (3): the X cells, every cell with k = 2) and every state that can survive one step leads to u (steps (1), (2), (4)), the law with λ > 0 is unique and positive. The two hypotheses are the geometric content, to be checked on each face.
lemma0
THEOREMS.md, Lemma 0: on a wrapped face Q is irreducible and aperiodic on L, every state outside L dies surely, every state is reachable from L.

The geometric steps of the proof are hypotheses: (2) singletons communicate, (3) a state u with M(u) = V, (4) u reachable from a singleton. Step (1) is the hypothesis of SubsetChain, proved for product kernels (ProductKernel.supp).
lemma0_qsd
Lemma 0: the quasi-stationary law is unique and charges every non-empty state.
Among laws with λ > 0 (see qsd_exists_unique).
death_pos

Follows from step (1) (∅ ⊆ M(x)).

Same, for any finite partition into differentiable positive rates with h_r' = -c_r h_r.
routes_second

Same, as the derivative of Σ p c.

Same.

Any finite number of exponential routes.
two_routes_step
Lemma R's discrete form, as corrected by the referee (REVIEW.md A3): ln τ(D+1) - ln τ(D) = c_s - ln(1 - p(D)(1 - e^{-(c_b - c_s)})).
Same; the source's c_s + p(c_b - c_s) is not this.
seam_identity
image/README.md: a torus is its cover conditioned on the seam's whole history recurring one loop along, divided by how likely that is: P_T(s₀..s_{m-1}) = P_C(s₀..s_{m-1}, s_m = s₀)/[π(s₀) Z].

The finite-K exact form, with (F^L)(s₀, s₀)/Tr F^N in place of π(s₀)·const, for F ≥ 0 and a cover a whole number of loops long. The factorisation of the history weight into a transfer matrix on bands two graph steps thick, and the cover having the same F, are the hypothesis (the ring weight), not derived from gump's rule. The referee measured that it also holds off multiples wherever (F^L)(a,a) > 0 (not formalised), and fails otherwise (2-cycle).
seam_identity_obs
(★): P_T(pattern on W) = P_C(pattern on W) · E_C[Q | pattern on W] / Z, for windows in the seam.
For the mean of any observable of the torus's cut configuration.
seam_sharp
REVIEW.md B, the sharp form for K = 2: P_C(seam = s₀, rest = s₁, image = s₀) = P_T(s₀, s₁) · P_T(seam = s₀).
Under Tr F^m = Tr F^{2m} = 1 (the referee's Z = 1 for a deterministic rule from a normalised soup), which is assumed, not derived.
cover_marginal

Same (Chapman–Kolmogorov, sum_pathF).
coverW_eq_ringL

Same.
thm3a
THEOREMS.md, Theorem 3 (a): under (SSM), |ln τ(G) - c_∞ A| ≤ K Σ_i e^{-r_i/ξ}.

With the referee's repair (an additive K₀), and from the integrated hypothesis IntSSM (|c_i(G) - c_∞| ≤ K e^{-r_i/ξ} + K₀/A), which is all the proof uses and which (SSM) implies (SSM.toIntSSM). r_i is any number attached to each cell.
SSM.toIntSSM
Theorem 3's hypothesis (SSM), uniform in s ∈ [0,1], with the referee's K₀/A.
Needs e_∞ integrable; redundant for every family with arbitrarily small error terms (SSM.toIntSSM_of_small).
thm3b
Theorem 3 (b): wrapped faces with shortest loop ℓ: |ln τ - c_∞ A| ≤ K A e^{-(ℓ-2)/2ξ}.
Plus K₀; the geometric fact r_i ≥ (ℓ - 2)/2 is the hypothesis.
thm3c
Theorem 3 (c): polygons: |ln τ - c_∞ A| ≤ K Σ_r n_r e^{-r/ξ} ≤ K′·(rim length).
Plus K₀; with integer distances and at most C·R cells at each distance as hypotheses, K′ = K C/(1 - e^{-1/ξ}).
thm3d
Theorem 3 (d): along a sequence with rim/A → 0 and ℓ → ∞, ln τ / A → c_∞, the same number for rimmed and wrapped faces.
Stated with A → ∞ and Σ_i e^{-r_i/ξ} = o(A) as the hypotheses.
tilt_riemann_bounds
(new; THEOREMS.md Theorem 2's monotonicity, used quantitatively) ln τ from finitely many tilted means.
New: (1/n)Σ_{k=1}^{n}⟨E⟩_{k/n} ≤ ln τ ≤ (1/n)Σ_{k=0}^{n-1}⟨E⟩_{k/n} on every face, a bracket of width ≤ ε_max A/n.
price_of_pointwise
(new; replaces (SSM) in Theorem 3 (d)) the price per cell from a bulk limit at each tilt.

New and weaker than (SSM): if ⟨E⟩_{s,G_n}/A_n → f(s) for every s ∈ (0,1] (no rate, no uniformity in s, no locality; jumps of f allowed), then ln τ/A → ∫₀¹ f. Two families have one price when their pointwise limits agree. Its hypothesis asks convergence at the jump point too; price_of_ae (the referee's) needs only almost every s.
SSM.einf_continuousOn
REVIEW.md A2.3 (the referee's argument): a jump of e_∞ makes (SSM) false, since every finite face's curve is continuous.
Same, as a theorem: (SSM) on a family with arbitrarily small error terms forces e_∞ continuous on [0,1].
price_compare
(new; the finite form of price_of_pointwise) two faces with the same per-cell tilted energy at finitely many tilts have nearly the same price.
New: if the per-cell curves differ by ≤ δ at s = k/n and each falls by ≤ w over [0,1], then |ln τ/A − ln τ′/A′| ≤ δ + w/n.
price_of_ae
(the referee's form of price_of_pointwise, taken over from ref-chain/RefChainVacuity.lean)
ln τ/A → ∫₀¹f from convergence of ⟨E⟩_{s,G_n}/A_n for almost every s ∈ (0,1]: a first-order jump costs nothing even if the finite curves do not converge at the jump point.
SSM.toIntSSM_of_small
(taken over from the referee) (SSM) gives IntSSM with no integrability hypothesis.
For families with arbitrarily small error terms. (Lean also has it under the referee's name SSM.toIntSSM'.)
SSM.tilt_limit
(taken over from the referee, RefChainSSM.lean) under (SSM) the per-cell tilted energy converges to e_∞ at every tilt.
Along families with A → ∞ and Σ_i e^{-r_i/ξ} = o(A).
jump_refutes_SSM
REVIEW.md A2.3 in full (taken over from the referee): a jump of the limiting per-cell tilted energy refutes (SSM).
For families with large faces and arbitrarily small error terms, whatever e_∞, K, K₀.
